doc.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Missing fun in jazz education
summary: Powell says bands re-creating Ellington lack fun and analysis makes the music cold.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Let me ask you a couple of questions about that. Do you think that in jazz education today that we’re missing something because there aren’t these funny little things that find their way into the music?
Give us an example or, or elaborate on that.

Okay. Bands, one of the main ingredients they’re missing, I play with some bands and I guess I shouldn’t name names. But we do maybe the 1940s Ellington book and so forth. We re-create that. The main ingredient that’s missing is fun. They don’t realize that those guys had fun. Those guys aren’t sitting up here analyzing every note and there’s a leading scholar now who conducts bands, and he explains an eighth note to you. That’s not necessary. There is a natural quality to the music. The music almost dictates to you how it should be played, if you let it. If you want to analyze it and put all of that, it comes out some very cold music because it doesn’t flow from a natural source.
